analyses.name: NVIDIA Corporation
analyses.verdict: Three months of sideways price against 85% revenue growth has compressed the multiple to 17.6x forward — the base is the opportunity, the earnings bar is the risk.

financials.summary: The datacenter segment remains effectively the entire story, dwarfing gaming, professional visualization and automotive combined. The Blackwell generation carried the year, with supply — not demand — the binding constraint throughout. Gross margins held in the mid-70s despite the mix shift toward complete rack-scale systems, which carry more bought-in content than merchant silicon. Free cash flow generation was large enough to fund both aggressive buybacks and the capital commitments behind the announced $500B domestic build plan. The balance sheet remains net-cash, which matters given how much of the AI complex is now financing capacity with debt.
highlights: Revenue growth +85.2% year-over-year
EPS growth +214.5% — operating leverage far outpacing the top line
Datacenter is the overwhelming majority of revenue; gaming is now a rounding error by comparison
Gross margin sustained in the mid-70s through the rack-scale mix shift
Forward P/E of 17.6x — a market multiple for the fastest-growing mega-cap
Net-cash balance sheet funding the $500B build commitment without leverage

accomplishments: Blackwell ramped to volume production and became the default training platform for frontier model builders
Announced a $500B domestic AI infrastructure build plan, moving from component supplier to infrastructure principal
Extended the CUDA software moat — the switching cost, not the silicon, remains the durable advantage
Reached a ~$5.46T market capitalisation, the largest company in the scanned universe
Networking (NVLink/InfiniBand/Ethernet) grew into a material second business rather than an accessory

journey_52w.summary: A year of two halves. The first was a powerful advance as Blackwell shipped and hyperscaler capex guidance kept ratcheting higher. The second has been a three-month consolidation — momentum is actually -4.3% over that window — as the market digested both the size of the $500B commitment and the credit implications of an industry funding capacity with debt. Price closed at 225.30, 4.3% below the 235.47 high, having ranged between 164.98 and 235.47 across the year. Critically, earnings compounded through the entire flat stretch, which is what took the forward multiple down to 17.6x.

That discount is the entire bull case — and it is also the market telling you it does not fully believe the durability.

analyses.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
analyses.verdict: A stock that has doubled in three months yet closed at an all-time high with RSI of only 59.9 — the most orderly major advance in the scan.

financials.summary: The Infrastructure Solutions Group has completely re-shaped the company. AI-optimised server demand drove revenue growth of 87.5% and EPS growth of 282.5%, converting Dell from a low-growth PC and enterprise-hardware business into the primary Western integrator of AI compute at rack scale. The important tension in the model is margin: AI servers carry substantially thinner gross margins than traditional enterprise storage and services, so revenue growth of this magnitude does not translate proportionally into gross profit. Management has offset that with scale, supply-chain leverage and attach of higher-margin storage and services. The Client Solutions Group (PCs) has been a steady but unexciting contributor.

EPS growth +282.5% — operating leverage despite thinner AI server margins
Infrastructure Solutions Group now the dominant revenue and growth driver
Forward P/E of 22.4x — modest against the growth rate

AI server backlog remains the key disclosed forward indicator

The advance has been unusually well-behaved: price is 17.6% above its 50-day (420.30) and 117% above its 200-day (227.44), yet RSI is only 59.9, meaning the gains came through sustained accumulation rather than a blow-off.

analyses.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
analyses.verdict: The unavoidable supplier for every AI chip, resting on its 50-day at a 19.8x multiple — the cheapest way to own the compute cycle.

financials.summary: Leading-edge nodes (3nm and below) drove the year, with high-performance computing displacing smartphones as the largest revenue platform — a structural shift, not a cyclical one. Revenue grew 36.0% and EPS 77.4%, with gross margins benefiting from both node mix and the pricing power that comes from being the only foundry able to produce at the frontier at scale. Advanced packaging (CoWoS) went from a bottleneck to a differentiated, capacity-constrained profit centre in its own right. Capital intensity remains extreme — overseas fab construction in Arizona, Japan and Germany carries a margin drag that management has been explicit about — but operating cash flow comfortably funds it.

analyses.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
analyses.verdict: 6.1x forward earnings against 1,368% EPS growth — the market is pricing a cycle top while the cycle is visibly still running.

financials.summary: An extraordinary year driven almost entirely by high-bandwidth memory. HBM is sold out well in advance, priced under long-term agreements, and carries margins far above commodity DRAM — which transformed the income statement. Revenue grew 345.7% and EPS 1,368.5%, figures that look like typos but reflect the operating leverage inherent in a memory business coming off a trough with pricing power. Conventional DRAM and NAND also benefited from constrained supply as capacity was redirected toward HBM. Capital expenditure rose sharply to fund HBM capacity, and management has been disciplined about not over-building conventional bit supply — the historic sin of the industry.

EPS growth +1,368.5% — the steepest earnings inflection in the scanned universe

analyses.name: Bank of America Corporation
analyses.verdict: The cleanest large-cap technical setup in the scan — 1.1% from its high with relative strength already at new highs, at 12.1x earnings.

financials.summary: Net interest income was the engine, benefiting from a rate environment that stayed higher for longer than the deposit base repriced. Revenue grew 16.8% and EPS 34.1%, with the EPS line further helped by a sustained buyback. Credit quality held up better than the bear case assumed — charge-offs normalised rather than deteriorated, and reserve builds were modest. The consumer bank continued to gather low-cost deposits, while Global Markets delivered a strong year on elevated volatility. Capital ratios remained comfortably above requirements, which is what funds the buyback that has been quietly compounding EPS.

analyses.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
analyses.verdict: All-time high, relative strength at new highs, TradingView's strongest energy rating — and still only 11.7x forward earnings.

financials.summary: An exceptional refining year. Crack spreads — the margin between crude input and refined product output — stayed elevated far longer than the forward curve had implied, and Marathon's scale and Gulf Coast positioning let it capture them fully. Revenue grew 53.7% and EPS 348%, the latter magnified by an aggressive buyback that has meaningfully shrunk the share count. The midstream affiliate (MPLX) continued to provide a stable, fee-based cash flow stream that partially offsets refining's volatility — a structural advantage over pure-play refiners. Capital returns remained the priority over growth capex, which is the correct posture at this point in the cycle.

analyses.name: Expeditors International of Washington
analyses.verdict: A 52-week-high close with a perfect TradingView reading — 17 buy signals, zero sell — and RSI still only 65.5.

financials.summary: An asset-light freight forwarder, which is the key to reading these numbers: Expeditors owns no aircraft or ships, so when airfreight volumes and rates rise, the incremental margin flows through with very little fixed cost absorbing it. Revenue grew 32.1% and EPS 51.5% — the gap between those two figures is the operating leverage of the model. Airfreight was the standout, with strong Q2 growth in particular. The balance sheet carries no meaningful debt and the company has a long history of returning excess cash. The counterpoint, well-flagged by sell-side commentary, is that the same asset-light model means there is no moat when volumes turn — the earnings fall as fast as they rose.

analyses.verdict: The best risk-adjusted setup on the board — a 90 score and a perfect TradingView rating with RSI at just 45.6, resting on its 50-day.

Dedicated Contract Services provided stable, contracted revenue that smooths the cyclicality of the spot-exposed segments. The brokerage business remains the most volatile piece. Capital expenditure moderated after prior-year container fleet investment, improving free cash flow conversion.

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: A $1.08T company growing revenue at 47.7% and closing 2.1% from its high with RSI at 52.3 — growth at scale without the crowding.

financials.summary: The incretin franchise — tirzepatide across both diabetes and obesity indications — dominated the year and remains the largest single growth driver in global pharmaceuticals. Revenue grew 47.7% and EPS 26.2%; the gap between the two reflects the enormous manufacturing capital being deployed to relieve supply constraints, which depresses near-term margins in exchange for future volume. Capacity expansion has been the central operational story: for much of the period, demand exceeded what Lilly could physically produce. The oncology and immunology portfolios provided secondary growth. Research and development spend remained elevated, funding both next-generation incretins and the Alzheimer's franchise.

EPS growth +26.2%, held below revenue growth by manufacturing capacity investment
Incretin franchise the dominant driver across diabetes and obesity
Manufacturing capacity, not demand, was the binding constraint for much of the year
Forward P/E of 25.6x — modest against 47.7% revenue growth
Elevated R&D funding next-generation incretins and the Alzheimer's programme

analyses.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
analyses.verdict: Three months of flat price against 242% EPS growth — the margin inflection is real and the base is well built.

financials.summary: The year the margin story finally arrived. Revenue grew 19.6% while EPS grew 242.3% — that gap is the entire investment case. Three things drove it: AWS reaccelerated as AI workloads moved from experimentation into production, the advertising business continued compounding at high incremental margins, and the North American retail cost structure benefited from the regionalised fulfilment network reaching maturity. AWS and advertising together now contribute the overwhelming majority of operating income despite being a minority of revenue. Capital expenditure rose sharply to fund AI datacenter capacity, which is the principal drag on free cash flow and the main thing bears point to.
highlights: Revenue growth +19.6% year-over-year
EPS growth +242.3% — the margin inflection is the story
AWS reaccelerated as AI workloads moved into production
Advertising continued compounding at high incremental margin
Regionalised fulfilment network delivered structural retail cost savings
Forward P/E of 25.5x on a ~$2.86T market capitalisation

analyses.name: Merck & Company, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The cheapest large-cap pharma making new highs — 14.2x forward earnings with a perfect TradingView reading.

financials.summary: A year defined by the tension between a dominant present and an uncertain future. Keytruda remained the largest-selling pharmaceutical product globally and continued expanding into earlier lines of therapy and adjuvant settings, driving the bulk of profitability. Revenue growth of 5.1% is modest — this is a mature franchise, not a growth story — but the cash generation is enormous and funds both the dividend and an active business-development programme aimed squarely at the post-Keytruda gap. The animal health business provided steady diversification. Management's central task, well understood by the market, is deploying that cash into assets that replace Keytruda revenue before loss of exclusivity arrives.

analyses.name: SpaceX
analyses.verdict: A new listing where the quant signals are structurally meaningless — judge the business, size the position small.

financials.summary: Two businesses in one listing, with very different characteristics. The launch business has effectively monopoly economics in commercial orbital launch: reusable boosters drove marginal cost per kilogram to a level no competitor has approached, and the manifest is booked out well in advance across commercial, civil and national-security customers. The far more important development is Starlink, which converts a lumpy, contract-driven project business into a recurring consumer and enterprise subscription business with a growing installed base — and increasingly direct-to-cell partnerships with terrestrial carriers. Revenue grew 91.9%. The capital intensity remains extreme: constellation replenishment is a permanent capital expenditure, not a one-time build.
highlights: Revenue growth +91.9% year-over-year
Reusable launch economics remain unmatched by any competitor
Starlink converts project revenue into recurring subscription revenue
Direct-to-cell carrier partnerships extend the addressable market beyond terminals
Forward P/E of 76.3x on a ~$1.86T implied market capitalisation
Constellation replenishment is a permanent, ongoing capital requirement

accomplishments: Completed one of the largest public listings on record
Sustained a launch cadence no competitor has come close to matching
Scaled Starlink into a material recurring-revenue business
Established direct-to-cell partnerships with terrestrial mobile carriers
Delivered 91.9% revenue growth at very substantial scale

journey_52w.summary: Too short a history for a genuine 52-week arc — that is the central analytical fact here. Since listing, the stock has traded between 108.27 and 211.39 and closed at 141.29, some 33.2% below its post-listing high and effectively on its still-forming 50-day at 141.85. The quant score of 45 reflects the absence of 52-week, VCP and relative-strength history rather than any bearish judgment; those signals are blank by construction for a new listing. TradingView does resolve a BUY, but on only 19 signals versus the 26 it uses for seasoned names — treat it as provisional.
